tasks.title: Bind runtime automatic updates to the project release signer identity
acceptance: automatic update rejects an MSI whose Authenticode chain is valid but whose signer is not an explicitly trusted HLS Downloader release signer
the expected signer identity comes from a versioned local trust contract rather than GitHub release metadata or another network-controlled field
the design supports deliberate certificate rotation without accepting arbitrary Windows-trusted code-signing certificates
existing SHA-256, size, exact product version, ProductName, UpgradeCode, per-user MSI and WinVerifyTrust checks remain fail-closed
Windows-focused automated coverage proves both accepted signer and wrong-signer rejection paths before merge

evidence.runtime_gap: native_shell/src/updater.rs verifies WinVerifyTrust and MSI identity but does not compare the signer to the formal release signer identity
evidence.formal_contract: scripts/sign-v7-authenticode.ps1 and verify-v7-authenticode.ps1 bind formal artifacts to HLS_V7_SIGN_CERT_THUMBPRINT

tasks.title: Enforce loopback-only Core TCP debug transport
acceptance: HLS_V7_CORE_BIND rejects every non-loopback IPv4 and IPv6 address rather than exposing the unauthenticated Core protocol to LAN or wildcard interfaces
default and explicitly configured loopback addresses continue to support test/Linux IPC
the Windows named-pipe owner/SYSTEM DACL and existing frame-size/read-timeout protections remain unchanged
automated tests cover 127.0.0.1, ::1, wildcard and representative private/public non-loopback addresses
no new unauthenticated remote transport is introduced

evidence.contract_mismatch: core_ipc.rs describes TCP as loopback test/Linux transport but default_core_bind accepts any SocketAddr from HLS_V7_CORE_BIND
evidence.impact: TCP dispatch has no session authentication and exposes full CorePipeRequest including command, settings, credential and shutdown operations

tasks.title: Prevent custom credential headers from crossing replay origins
acceptance: cross-origin replay does not forward arbitrary source-origin custom headers by default, including X-Api-Key/X-Auth-Token style credentials
same-origin replay keeps required captured custom headers and exact origin-scoped request_contexts may explicitly restore headers only for their matching origin
Cookie/Authorization/Proxy-Authorization protections and request_context cookie isolation remain fail-closed
the solution uses an allowlist or explicit origin-scoped ownership model rather than an incomplete denylist of guessed secret header names
tests cover same-origin custom header replay, unscoped cross-origin stripping, exact scoped cross-origin restoration, and existing HLS/CDN replay behavior

evidence.extension_capture: RequestChainStore captures arbitrary request headers; replayableRequestHeaders removes hop-by-hop/cookie/proxy headers but permits custom headers
evidence.core_replay: apply_replay_json_for strips only Cookie, Authorization and Proxy-Authorization when _task_url origin differs; existing test intentionally retains X-Playback across origins
evidence.impact: custom credential headers can be replayed to an unscoped cross-origin child unless that header happens to be one of the three explicitly stripped names
